title: Forest classification supports a newly resolved neutron-star candidate
summary: MUWCLASS assigned the newly resolved X-ray source CXO J170144.5–421415 a neutron-star class probability of 66%. This is an object-specific candidate interpretation, not confirmation of its identity or association with HESS J1702–420A. Chandra imaging resolved the object conventionally.
organization: IRAP; George Washington University; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

evidence.tested: Forest trained on approximately 3,000 literature-classed sources, applied to 18 field sources. Src11 probability 66%, confidence statistic 1.20.
evidence.unknown: Only 17 Src11 photons and poorly constrained spectrum; identity and PeVatron association remain unconfirmed. The classifier mislabels another likely cataclysmic variable because relevant variability/spectral-line features are omitted. Earlier PWN interpretation concerned the unresolved region.
evidence.ai_role: The forest combines X-ray and multiwavelength features to provide a new object-specific candidate class, separate from conventional imaging.

source_review.scope: Primary Sections2.2 and3.2: newly resolved identity versus earlier unresolved interpretation, classifier Methods and result; current v1 date.
